item.title: China’s CXMT eyes NAND flash expansion as AI drives memory shortage
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: China’s CXMT is preparing an R&D production line for NAND flash memory, broadening beyond DRAM as AI infrastructure contributes to a global memory shortage.
item.content:encoded:
Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies is preparing to move into NAND flash, expanding beyond its core DRAM business as artificial-intelligence infrastructure drives tighter supplies across the global memory market, Reuters reported.

The company plans to establish a research-and-development production line for NAND chips at a new Beijing facility and has started discussions with potential customers, including an unnamed AI-focused startup, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.

CXMT moves beyond DRAM

CXMT has built its position primarily in DRAM, the type of memory used in servers, personal computers and other computing systems. NAND flash is used for non-volatile storage in products ranging from solid-state drives and smartphones to data-center storage systems.

An entry into NAND would place CXMT in competition with global suppliers including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, while also bringing it closer to domestic rival Yangtze Memory Technologies, which has focused on NAND.

CXMT and YMTC have often been described as two of China’s most important memory-chip companies, but their product focus has historically kept them in different segments. A NAND push by CXMT would narrow that separation as both companies expand during a period of unusually strong memory demand.

AI demand tightens memory supply

The planned expansion comes as AI servers consume larger amounts of memory and storage, contributing to supply constraints that are affecting data centers, smartphones and personal computers. Reuters separately reported this week that smaller device makers are preparing for years of memory scarcity as suppliers prioritize higher-value products and AI infrastructure.

For memory manufacturers, the shortage creates an incentive to add capacity while also making technology mix more important. AI infrastructure relies heavily on high-bandwidth memory and DRAM, but NAND demand also rises as training and inference systems generate and store larger datasets.

CXMT’s move would therefore broaden the company’s exposure to an AI-driven memory cycle while giving China another domestic supplier in a segment that remains dominated by overseas companies.

China’s memory makers raise capital for expansion

CXMT raised about $8.6 billion in a 2026 initial public offering, giving it additional capital to expand research and manufacturing. Reuters reported that the parent of YMTC is also preparing for a Shanghai listing.

Both companies are part of China’s broader effort to strengthen domestic semiconductor supply chains as US export controls restrict access to some advanced chipmaking equipment and AI processors. Memory remains strategically important because modern computing systems require both processing capacity and increasingly large pools of fast memory and storage.

The NAND plan is still under development. Reuters reported that CXMT is preparing an R&D production line rather than announcing a full commercial capacity target, and the company has not publicly detailed a production timetable or expected output.

If it progresses from research into volume production, CXMT’s expansion would add another competitive variable to a memory market already being reshaped by AI demand, capacity constraints and efforts by major economies to localize semiconductor manufacturing.

item.title: Singlife says Salesforce AI agents cut handling time 30%, training time by half
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singlife says its Salesforce-powered AI agents are producing measurable customer-service gains, including 30 percent lower handling time and 50 percent shorter training for new hires.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore insurer Singlife says its use of Salesforce AI agents is beginning to show measurable operating results, with one customer-service agent handling more than 20 percent of email enquiries and another cutting average handling time by 30 percent.

The update builds on Singlife’s deployment of its internal AI agent Buddy, which TNGlobal covered in October 2025. According to new materials shared by Salesforce and Singlife, Buddy has also reduced training time for new customer-service hires by 50 percent, taking onboarding from four weeks to two.

Email agent handles more than one-fifth of enquiries

Singlife’s General Insurance Email Agent assesses incoming customer emails in real time, identifies the nature and urgency of each request, and routes the enquiry to the appropriate support path. Straightforward questions can receive an immediate response, while more complex or sensitive cases are escalated to human agents.

The insurer said the system now handles more than 20 percent of customer enquiries received by email. During a period of increased email volume earlier this year, Singlife said it was able to resolve most email enquiries within two days.

The operating model illustrates a common approach to customer-facing AI deployment: automate routine classification and responses while keeping human escalation available for cases that require judgment, sensitivity or more complex policy handling.

Buddy moves toward customer-facing use

Buddy was introduced last year to support Singlife customer-service executives with real-time responses to internal questions. The latest update says the agent has reduced average handling time by 30 percent and cut new-hire training time in half.

Singlife plans to move Buddy beyond its current employee-assistance role and develop it into a customer-facing digital agent. The insurer said policyholders would eventually be able to use it across digital channels to access policy information and complete routine self-service requests.

That shift will place more emphasis on how the system handles identity, permissions, escalation and the boundary between routine self-service and decisions that require an employee. It will also provide a clearer test of whether the productivity gains reported internally translate into a better customer experience when the agent is exposed directly to policyholders.

ASEAN enterprises move from pilots to operating metrics

Salesforce has been highlighting production deployments across Southeast Asia as it expands Agentforce and related AI interfaces. The Singlife figures are useful because they move the discussion from product availability toward operating measures such as handling time, training time, enquiry share and service levels.

For Singlife, the next phase will be less about whether an AI agent can answer questions and more about how reliably it can work within insurance-service controls as its role expands. The performance figures in the latest update were supplied by Salesforce and Singlife and have not been independently audited by TNGlobal.

item.title: Ant International rolls out AI-native stack across payments, FX, treasury and credit
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Ant International has unveiled an AI-native financial stack spanning payments, accounts, FX, treasury, credit and merchant growth across its Alipay+, Antom, WorldFirst and Bettr businesses.
item.content:encoded:
Ant International has unveiled a broad AI-native product stack spanning payments, business accounts, foreign exchange, treasury, credit and merchant growth, extending its agentic-finance push beyond individual payment tools into day-to-day financial operations.

The company said the upgrade includes close to 100 products across its Alipay+, Antom, WorldFirst and Bettr businesses. The stack is built around two proprietary models: the Antom 3-in-1 Transformer for payment data and FalconTST for foreign-exchange and liquidity forecasting. Ant International said the products will roll out to global markets through fall and winter 2026.

AI moves deeper into payment operations

Ant International is positioning Antom Autopilot as a conversational layer across the merchant payment lifecycle, including onboarding, integration, orchestration, fraud protection, revenue recovery, troubleshooting, reconciliation and market expansion. The company said merchants using AI integration quadrupled over the past 12 months and expects 95 percent of merchants to be able to onboard new payment methods within one hour by the end of 2026.

The company also introduced or expanded tools for dispute management, payment routing, retries, wallet checkout and agentic transactions. Ant International said 89.5 percent of merchants using its Antom service have deployed AI agents and that AI assists 81.4 percent of payment tasks. Those figures are company-reported.

The underlying Antom 3-in-1 Transformer has more than 10 billion parameters and is designed to process sequential, tabular and graph data in one architecture. Ant International said the model processes 90 trillion data points annually and is used across fraud, scam and abuse prevention as well as payment optimization.

WorldFirst adds AI-native account and treasury workflows

For business accounts, WorldFirst is adding natural-language and agent-based workflows for onboarding, account management, payments and treasury. Its Wyn assistant is aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises, while WorldFirst for Enterprise is adding supervised agentic workflows for compliance, eKYC and KYB, payment management and treasury.

The treasury stack includes World Map for cash visibility, Falcon Forecast for cash-flow and foreign-exchange forecasting, Falcon FX for dynamic pricing and hedging recommendations, Whale Pooling for liquidity movement, and World Payout for selecting payout routes based on factors including cost, success rate, speed and risk.

Ant International said FalconTST has more than 8.5 billion parameters and has achieved more than 93 percent accuracy in foreign-exchange and cash-flow forecasting in its own real-world cases. It also claims the model reduced corporate FX hedging and allocation costs by 30 percent to 60 percent in those cases.

Agentic commerce and credit expand the stack

Ant International is also pushing AI into commerce and embedded finance. The product set includes an Agentic Commerce Hub for distributing product catalogs to third-party agent platforms, a shopping agent for direct-to-consumer experiences, and upgraded A+Rewards tools for cross-channel customer acquisition.

Bettr’s AI Credit Engine, meanwhile, is being used by partners to provide credit services to small businesses. Ant International said the system supports 49 institutions in 28 markets with access to more than 100 million users, while Bettr Global Credit can return credit decisions in as little as one minute.

The release builds on Ant International’s earlier work around the Alipay+ Agentic Mobile Protocol and know-your-agent controls. TNGlobal previously reported that Ant International, Mastercard and Visa were working toward interoperable standards for identifying and governing AI agents in payment environments.

The larger question for global businesses will be how much autonomy they are prepared to give these systems as AI moves from recommendations into payments, treasury movements, credit decisions and account operations. Ant International says its architecture keeps permissions and governance embedded in those workflows, while many of the performance figures released with the new stack remain vendor-reported and will need to be judged against broader production use.

item.title: Korea’s ITM Semiconductor recovers $2.5M out of $9.3M embezzlement in Vietnam
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: South Korea's ITM Semiconductor recovered about KRW3.5 billion ($2.47 million) out of an employee embezzlement worth KRW13.2 billion at its Vietnamese subsidiary ITM Semiconductor Vietnam.
item.content:encoded:
South Korea’s ITM Semiconductor recovered about KRW3.5 billion ($2.47 million) out of an employee embezzlement worth KRW13.2 billion at its Vietnamese subsidiary ITM Semiconductor Vietnam.

In its annual report for 2025, ITM Semiconductor said after the recovery, the outstanding KRW9.7 billion won ($6.8 million) was recorded as a receivable from illegal acts and written down in full. ITM Semiconductor highlighted significant uncertainty over whether the money can be retrieved.

The company reported the case to Vietnamese authorities in January 2026 and a police investigation is under way. On discovering the scheme, ITM Semiconductor conducted an internal investigation and judged the likelihood of further losses to be low.

The fraud was only a fraction of a much larger deterioration at the unit. ITM Semiconductor Vietnam reported a net loss of about KRW85.7 billion won on revenue of KRW174 billion won. The net loss in 2025 was worse than KRW20.8 billion a year earlier, according to the financial statement.

ITM Semiconductor makes protection components for rechargeable batteries and runs manufacturing operations in Vietnam, China, and other countries.

Vietnam records foreign investment $14.2B in semiconductor, to further attract big tech

item.title: Singapore’s Thunes launches cross-border payouts across six new Middle East markets
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Thunes, the Singapore-based payment firm, has announced a major expansion of its Direct Global Network across the Middle East.
item.content:encoded:
Thunes, the Singapore-based payment firm, has announced a major expansion of its Direct Global Network across the Middle East.

The expansion introduces new payout services into six key markets: the Kingdom of Bahrain, Lebanon, the Sultanate of Oman, South Yemen, Syria and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the firm said in a statement on Monday.

This move significantly enhances Thunes’ cross-border infrastructure in the region, delivering faster, highly transparent payment solutions for Members of Thunes’ Direct Global Network.

Members can now process payouts to millions of bank accounts, mobile wallets, and cash pickup locations in local currencies throughout the region, either through direct API integration with Thunes or by leveraging existing Swift connectivity.

The regional rollout builds on Thunes’ expansion of real-time payments across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in September 2025 and targets diverse economic needs across the Middle East, including powering digital economies, fueling enterprise and consumer growth, delivering vital remittance lifelines.

In Bahrain, where the non-oil sector contributed 85 percent of real gross domestic product (GDP) in 2025, Thunes supports direct bank payouts aligned with the nation’s National Digital Economy Strategy.

In Oman, bank account payouts support the digital transformation goals of Oman Vision 2040 alongside projected GDP growth of 4 percent in 2026.

In the UAE, a primary regional payments hub driven by the National Payment Systems Strategy (NPSS), Thunes now supports bank account payouts for both consumers and enterprises.

In markets relying on remittance flows for economic resilience and recovery, Thunes provides critical access points to Lebanon, South Yemen and Syria/

For Lebanon, the firm is supporting mobile wallet payouts in a market receiving roughly $7 billion per year in remittances.

For South Yemen, the firm is enabling bank and cash pickup payouts where remittances represent over 38 percent of its total GDP, ranking among the top three most remittance-dependent nations globally.

As for Syria, the firm is introducing payouts to cash pickup locations, providing reliable financial access amid broader efforts to rebuild the local banking system.

“Launching new payout capabilities across the Middle East unlocks significant value for our Members and their end-users,

“These markets are deeply committed to digital innovation and financial inclusion. Thunes is proud to provide the infrastructure that empowers businesses and individuals to participate seamlessly in international commerce and the broader global economy,” said Chloé Mayenobe, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Thunes.

With this expansion, Thunes said it reinforces its position as a leading provider of global money movement.

The solutions leverage Thunes’ in-house SmartX Treasury System for AI-driven forecasting and real-time liquidity management, and its Fortress Compliance Platform, which benefits from over 50 licenses worldwide, ensuring that every payment is executed with the highest levels of security, compliance and operational efficiency, said the statement.

item.title: Singapore’s dtcpay extends $25M Series A funding round with SBI investment
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Dtcpay, a Singapore-based payment, announced Friday the extension of its $25 million Series A funding round with SBI Group as its strategic investor.
item.content:encoded:
Dtcpay, a Singapore-based payment, announced Friday the extension of its $25 million Series A funding round with SBI Group as its strategic investor.

The firm said in a statement the round which was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India in April 2026, is now further anchored by the Japan’s financial conglomerate, which is investing both through its subsidiary, SBI Ventures Asset Pte Ltd, and through the SBI-NTU-Kyobo Digital Innovation Fund.

The round also drew participation from Genedant Capital and existing investor, Kwee Liong Tek, a prominent Singaporean business leader.

This additional fundraise enables dtcpay to maintain its pace of execution, scaling its product suite and merchant network while extending its lead in stablecoin payments.

It continues to invest in its product roadmap through the remaining half of 2026, including a revamped business portal for enterprise clients and a series of new consumer-friendly features rolled out within the dtcpay app.

The completion of the Series A also brings together a diverse group of investors whose collective expertise spans traditional finance, fintech infrastructure, and global market expansion.

Beyond capital, these investors contribute strategic network and domain expertise that will help support the company’s next phase of growth.

Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India, part of Vertex Holdings, a wholly owned subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, led the initial tranche of the round.

In addition to capital, Vertex brings extensive experience scaling technology companies, providing valuable strategic guidance rooted in deep Southeast Asian market expertise.

SBI Group adds a compelling financial service and fintech pedigree to the shareholder base. As one of Japan’s largest financial services groups, SBI operates across banking, securities, insurance, asset management, and digital assets. It has also been among the most active institutional investors in fintech and digital asset infrastructure globally.

Completing the investor group is Genedant Capital, a Singapore-based fund management firm licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore with over USD 2 billion in assets under management and advisory, and existing investor, Kwee Liong Tek.

Genedant Capital brings in a network of family offices, private wealth investors and institutional relationships across Asia, strengthening access to strategic capital as dtcpay scales internationally.

Kwee continues to increase his commitment, reflecting his long-term conviction in the company’s vision of bringing regulated digital payment infrastructure to global markets.

“SBI Group has spent decades shaping financial infrastructure across Japan and beyond, from banking and securities to blockchain and digital assets, and their conviction in dtcpay is validation that compliant, real-world stablecoin payments are not a distant vision but an infrastructure being built right now,

“Combined with the enduring trust of Kwee and the support of Genedant Capital, we have the capital, the network, and the momentum to move into every market that is ready for this change. And we are just getting started.” said Alice Liu, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of dtcpay.

Band Zhao, Group Chairman of dtcpay, said the next chapter for dtcpay is about scale.

“We are strengthening our infrastructure, deepening partnerships with global financial institutions, and expanding into new regulated markets to make stablecoin payments as seamless and trusted as traditional payment rails,

“With the backing of our investors, we are accelerating our mission to build the financial infrastructure that enables businesses and consumers to move value globally, instantly, and compliantly,” he added.

Eiichiro So, CEO of SBI Ven Capital, said this investment marks the beginning of a strategic partnership with dtcpay.

“It also reflects our broader view to expand the global corridor for digital asset origination between Japan and Southeast Asia through trusted, regulated digital financial infrastructure,” he added.

Meanwhile, Quek How Jiang, Chief Executive Officer of Genedant Capital, sees dtcpay is building the regulated infrastructure that will bring stablecoin payments into everyday commerce.

“Beyond capital, we look forward to leveraging our network of strategic investors, industry leaders and institutional relationships to support the company’s commercial expansion and international growth,” he added.

item.title: Green SM launches electric motorbike service in Indonesia
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Green SM has launched its electric motorbike service in Jakarta, expanding its all-electric transportation ecosystem in Indonesia to include two-wheeled mobility alongside electric taxis.
item.content:encoded:
Green SM has launched its electric motorbike service in Jakarta, expanding its all-electric transportation ecosystem in Indonesia to include two-wheeled mobility alongside electric taxis.

The company said in a statement on Thursday that the service is aimed at meeting the daily transportation needs of Jakarta residents, with a focus on convenience, safety, fleet quality and transparent pricing.

Jakarta, one of the region’s most dynamic cities, has strong demand for motorbike-based transportation, making flexible and efficient mobility options important for urban residents, Green SM said.

The company will deploy fully electric VinFast motorbikes and operate the service with a professional and trained driver team. Customers can book rides through the Green SM app, either through standard ride-hailing or the Green Now feature for faster bookings.

The expansion will also provide new income opportunities for two-wheel service drivers through flexible rental arrangements, Green SM said.

Under its rent-to-own option, drivers can rent a vehicle from IDR39,000 per day, with guaranteed earnings of up to IDR160,000 per day and the opportunity to own the vehicle after two years.

Green SM Global Chief Executive Officer Pham Nhat Minh Hoang said the Jakarta launch was a strategic step in the company’s international expansion.

“We aim to build a comprehensive fully electric mobility ecosystem encompassing both electric cars and electric motorbikes, enabling us to meet a broader range of everyday mobility needs,” he said.

Hoang said Green SM also sought to be a long-term partner to Indonesia in its green transition and emissions reduction efforts.

According to vehicle life-cycle assessments cited by Green SM, electric cars and motorbikes can generate about 75 percent lower emissions than gasoline-powered vehicles.

Globally, Green SM has completed about 850 million rides covering nearly 6 billion kilometres, helping reduce more than 800,000 tons of carbon dioxide emissions, the company said.

With the addition of electric motorbikes in Indonesia, Green SM said it was strengthening its green mobility ecosystem by offering electric taxis for longer journeys and electric motorbikes for faster and more flexible urban travel.

item.title: ResponsAbility commits up to $25M to back Verdant Energy’s renewable energy growth across Thailand
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Switzerland-based investment firm responsAbility will provide up to $25 million in non-recourse project financing, on behalf of its investors, to support the expansion of Verdant Energy’s solar portfolio in Thailand.
item.content:encoded:
Switzerland-based investment firm responsAbility will provide up to $25 million in non-recourse project financing, on behalf of its investors, to support the expansion of Verdant Energy’s solar portfolio in Thailand.

The transaction forms part of responsAbility’s $500 million climate investment strategy for Asia, a private debt strategy focused on climate infrastructure across emerging and developing markets and supporting scalable private-sector infrastructure solutions that contribute to decarbonization, responsAbility said in a statement on Wednesday.

Headquartered in Singapore, Verdant Energy develops, constructs, owns and operates renewable energy assets across Southeast Asia, with offices in Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines.

“This transaction is fully aligned with responsAbility’s strategy of supporting scalable renewable energy companies that contribute to decarbonisation while addressing growing energy demand in emerging markets,

“Verdant’s strong execution track record, scalable business model, and presence in Thailand, a market with attractive renewable energy growth prospects, make it a compelling partner for advancing clean energy deployment in the region,” said Jay Bathija, Principal, Climate Infrastructure Investments at responsAbility.

Alan Yau, Chief Executive Officer of Verdant Energy, said Southeast Asia is at the forefront of the global energy transition, driven by rapid economic growth and increasing demand for reliable, affordable and sustainable power.

“At Verdant Energy, our vision is to be a leading regional renewable energy platform by partnering with governments, customers, and capital providers to accelerate the deployment of high-quality clean energy infrastructure,

“This collaboration with responsAbility further strengthens our financial capacity to scale our portfolio and contribute meaningfully to the region’s decarbonization journey,” he added.

Sivaramakrishnan Sreedharan, Chief Investment Officer of Verdant Energy, said access to long-term, flexible project capital is essential to scaling renewable energy infrastructure.

“This facility enables us to accelerate the delivery of bankable projects while maintaining the disciplined investment and risk management principles that underpin Verdant Energy’s growth strategy across Southeast Asia,” he added.

ResponsAbility said this facility underscores its commitment to deploying capital from its $500 million Climate Investment Strategy for Asia, which is dedicated to accelerating decarbonization across emerging and developing markets in the region.

By backing scalable platforms such as Verdant Energy, the firm aims to support the build-out of critical renewable energy infrastructure while mobilizing private capital towards Asia’s energy transition.

ResponsAbility closes Asia Climate Fund at $461M

item.title: Singapore says AI safeguards must keep pace with technology
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Singapore will continue to strengthen safeguards for artificial intelligence (AI) as the technology becomes more capable, with Communications and Information Minister Josephine Teo saying safety measures must develop alongside adoption.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore will continue to strengthen safeguards for artificial intelligence (AI) as the technology becomes more capable, with Communications and Information Minister Josephine Teo saying safety measures must develop alongside adoption.

Teo said trust was essential for any technology to be regularly relied upon, drawing a comparison with civil aviation, where extensive standards and regulations govern aircraft manufacturing, servicing, airspace and airport management.

“We expect companies in the world of civil aviation to each do their part to train their people properly and implement safeguards consistently,” Teo said in a LinkedIn post on Thursday.

She said AI would similarly need its own safety mechanisms, although these were still taking shape and were far from mature.

“More research and testing is needed. This takes time and commitment,” she said, adding that Singapore must undertake the practical work of building safeguards as AI adoption grows.

This includes developing ways to test and assure AI systems, strengthening technical capabilities to evaluate advanced models and providing organizations with practical guidance on responsible use, Teo said.

She cited initiatives including AI Verify, the Singapore AI Safety Institute and Singapore’s Model AI Governance Frameworks as part of the country’s efforts to develop AI safeguards.

Teo also said international cooperation was necessary because AI safety could not be addressed by any country alone.

The International Scientific Exchange for AI Safety, which brings together perspectives from around the world, had helped identify shared priorities for global AI safety research through the Singapore Consensus, she said.

“We will not have all the answers from the outset. But as AI grows more capable, its safeguards must keep pace,” Teo said.

Singapore will continue to test, learn and strengthen its approach, while working with industry, researchers and international partners to support the use of AI with confidence, she added.

JTC and Kajima launch Singapore’s first autonomous heavy construction equipment pilot to ease manpower constraints, improve worksite safety

item.title: JTC and Kajima launch Singapore’s first autonomous heavy construction equipment pilot to ease manpower constraints, improve worksite safety
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: JTC Corporation, Singapore’s industrial land and infrastructure agency, and Kajima Corporation, Japan’s construction company, have launched the first pilot project to explore the use of autonomous heavy construction equipment in Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
JTC Corporation, Singapore’s industrial land and infrastructure agency, and Kajima Corporation, Japan’s construction company, have launched the first pilot project to explore the use of autonomous heavy construction equipment in Singapore.

Held at Jurong Innovation District, these autonomous machines, starting with excavators and compactors, will be tested at the Bulim Autonomous Yard (BAY), JTC’s sandbox for validating autonomous construction equipment under real site conditions, the duo said in a statement on Thursday.

Together with the Public Sector Science & Technology Policy & Plans Office (S&TPPO) and the Housing & Development Board (HDB), this pilot will test how these machines can ease Singapore’s construction manpower constraints and improve safety.

Since 2025, JTC has been mandating the use of robotics in construction tenders to achieve higher productivity in the sector.

Under the trial, an operator assigns tasks and sets virtual geographic boundaries (geofencing) for each autonomous construction machine.

Using sensors and artificial intelligence, the machine then carry out the tasks independently, without an operator in the cabin or elsewhere.

The activities are monitored remotely by staff who will intervene whenever an issue occurs. JTC is targeting a reduction of operator manpower by half, with one operator overseeing two machines.

The pilot will draw on technologies from multiple technology partners. To automate digging, the excavator uses a retrofit kit from Gravis Robotics, a Zurich-based startup that develops autonomous software and hardware for earthmoving equipment.

Similarly, the compactor runs on Kajima’s A4CSEL, its first deployment outside Japan. Retrofitting is an important design feature that lowers the barrier to adoption, as contractors can upgrade machines they already own, rather than replace entire fleets.

“Adding more manpower is not a sustainable way to meet Singapore’s future construction needs. JTC has a pipeline of at least 800 hectares of earthworks projects over the next five years,

“If the pilot succeeds, we will deploy autonomous heavy construction equipment across suitable projects in our pipeline and support wider industry adoption,” said Calvin Chung, Assistant Chief Executive Officer, Engineering & Operations Group, JTC.

According to the statement, autonomous construction equipment has the added advantage of reducing workers’ exposure to some onsite safety hazards by decreasing the need for personnel to operate machinery or work in close proximity to moving equipment.

Arising from the BAY trials, JTC is working with Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to develop operating guidelines and safeguards to support industry-wide deployment while prioritizing human safety.

These include geofencing to keep machines within designated areas, LiDAR sensors to detect humans and obstacles, and emergency-stop controls on site and in the control room.

JTC and Kajima will also explore extending the trial to autonomous bulldozers and dump trucks in 2027, creating a coordinated fleet of machines.

“Through close collaboration with JTC and our local partners, we will advance the development of automated construction technologies that enhance productivity, safety and quality, while addressing the challenges facing Singapore’s construction industry,

“We believe the combination of Kajima’s technologies and Singapore’s innovation-driven environment will help realize the next generation of construction,” Mr Yoshihiko Riho, Senior Executive Officer, Kajima Corporation, said Yoshihiko Riho, Senior Executive Officer, Kajima Corporation.

It is noted that scaling autonomous construction will require new skills in data interpretation, digital task planning, system integration and maintenance.

As these capabilities are nascent in Singapore, Kajima is working with local contractor Kok Tong Construction and equipment provider Tractors Singapore Limited to retrofit conventional equipment with autonomous capabilities, train Singapore-based operators and engineers, and document lessons from the pilot for wider industry adoption.

Beyond the pilot, JTC will be collaborating with public agencies, contractors, equipment providers, research institutions, and technology companies to conduct more autonomous construction trials at the BAY sandbox, said the statement.
